verdict: No: the spec makes everything the agent writes deterministic (stamped ids, closed events, validated handoffs) but leaves what the agent receives to chance - the SessionStart output has no bound, no order and nothing covering compaction, the hooks are never checked at runtime, and no channel tells the agent the gate outcome, its egress or its own recent failures; the largest gap is that the host-to-agent channel is not modeled at all (01 1.2).

findings.defect: The SessionStart output of `julieta handoff show --hook` has no size bound, no order and no truncation rule, so the context the first turn depends on can bury the narrative or flood the window.
findings.scenario: A project six months old has 300 open entries, 80 entries tagged `lesson` (03 3.9 prints every one, done or not, every session) and 40 recorded hook failures; SessionStart prints all of it in an unspecified order, the human-written narrative lands in the middle, and the agent acts on the first screen of warnings and never reads the Next steps.
findings.change: In 08 8.2 fix the order (narrative first, then the facts diff, then warnings, then entries) and a bound for the whole output (a starting value in a 13 13.8-style table, for example 8 KiB), with a fixed truncation line that names the command printing the rest (`julieta memory list --json`, `julieta status`); print only open `lesson` entries, newest first, up to a count; add a golden in 10 10.1 for the truncated case.
findings.cost: One paragraph and one starting value in 08 8.2, one golden test; a decision on the bound.

findings.defect: Only `/clear` (SessionEnd then SessionStart) is covered; context compaction and session resume, the most common ways an agent loses its context, have no hook, so handoff, warnings and lessons are never re-asserted after them.
findings.scenario: Two hours into a session, auto-compaction summarizes the SessionStart block away; the warning 'snapshots disabled for shop-web' and the open entry about a flaky arm64 test survive only as paraphrase or not at all; the agent repeats the work the entry recorded and commits in the repo whose snapshots are off.
findings.change: In 08 8.2 and 06 6.4 wire SessionStart for the compact and resume sources too (and a PreCompact hook if the pinned version has one) to the same `handoff show --hook`; add a sandbox probe row in 11 11.2 that records which sources the pinned Claude Code fires and that the output reaches the context.
findings.cost: Two hook entries in the `julieta-claude` kit, one probe row, one container e2e case.

findings.defect: What happens when a session hook fails is unspecified (exit status semantics, whether stderr reaches the agent, where the failure is recorded), and no probe measures that hook stdout enters the agent's context in the pinned version.
findings.scenario: `julieta setup` failed on a fresh sandbox, so `$HOME/.local/bin/julieta` does not exist (02 2.5, 06 6.4); the operator starts the agent anyway; SessionStart fails with 'not found', Claude Code shows it to the operator's terminal or nowhere, and the agent starts with no handoff, no entries and no warnings, believing the project is new.
findings.change: In 08 8.2 state the exit status each hook returns on failure and what it prints on stdout in that case (one line naming the failure and `julieta status`), and invoke the hooks by the absolute `.romeu/bin` path rather than through the setup-made link; add a C-row in 11 11.2 that records, for the pinned version, stdout injection, any size limit, behavior on non-zero exit and the SessionEnd timeout.
findings.cost: A paragraph in 08 8.2, one probe row, one container e2e case.

findings.defect: Nothing checks at runtime that the SessionStart and SessionEnd hooks and the two skills are wired; S5 is measured once in B2, and a personal kit that carries 'personal agent context' (06 6.5) can replace them with no precedence rule.
findings.scenario: A personal kit installs its own Claude Code settings file after `julieta-claude` (kits keep their order, 03 3.2); the hooks are gone; every session starts blind and no warning appears anywhere, because the warning channel is the hook that was removed.
findings.change: Add to `julieta setup` and `julieta status` (04 4.3) a check that the agent's settings carry the two hooks with julieta's exact commands and that both skills are present, reported as a warning in `romeu status` (which reads `julieta status --json`); state in 06 6.5 that a personal kit may not replace `julieta-claude`'s hooks, and test it.
findings.cost: One check in julieta-core, one warning id, one container e2e case.

findings.defect: The spec makes the agent's own memory dir non-writable but never says what the agent sees when its habitual write fails, or what tells it at that moment to use `julieta memory`; SessionStart warns only in the opposite case (writable or not empty, 08 8.2).
findings.scenario: The agent decides to remember a convention, writes to its built-in memory, gets a permission error, and improvises: it writes a NOTES.md in the repo, which then gets committed, or it retries elsewhere under $HOME, outside every mount, so the note dies with the sandbox.
findings.change: In 08 8.1 ('How julieta replaces the agent's built-in memory') require SessionStart to print one fixed line every session saying built-in memory is disabled and naming `julieta memory add`; have C3 (11 11.2) record the error text the pinned version shows on a refused memory write, so the guide and the skill can name it.
findings.cost: One line of hook output, one probe observation.

findings.defect: The hook dispatcher stops at the first non-zero of three stages but nothing says what it prints (which stage failed, the hook file, the fix), and every failure, including a normal refusal, is shown at each SessionStart until the same hook next succeeds (08 8.2).
findings.scenario: A commit fails; the agent sees only the failing program's own output and cannot tell julieta's `lock --check` from the repo's `.githooks/pre-commit` from `$GIT_DIR/hooks/pre-commit`; it edits the wrong one. Separately, a pre-push refused for a dirty tree stays listed as a hook failure in every session until the next successful push, so real failures blend into normal refusals.
findings.change: In 04 4.3 require the dispatcher to print, on stderr before exiting, one line `julieta hooks: <hook> stage <julieta|tracked|local> (<path>) exited <n>` plus the julieta error id and fix when the stage is julieta's own; in 08 8.2 show at SessionStart only failures since the last narrative handoff, newest first, within the L5-1 bound.
findings.cost: One output line and one rule in two sections; a test row.

findings.defect: The narrative kinds `clear` and `final` exist only when the operator remembers to type `/handoff`; `stop` and `recreate` give the running agent no notice, `rm` only warns, and nothing says what SessionStart shows when the newest facts have no narrative after them.
findings.scenario: The operator runs `romeu recreate shop` while the agent is mid-task; salvage stops the agent (08 8.5), no `final` handoff exists, `rm` printed a warning that scrolled by, and the next session sees an old narrative from three days ago presented as the latest, with no sign that a whole session's reasoning is missing.
findings.change: In 08 8.3 make SessionStart say, when the newest `facts` is newer than the latest narrative, 'no narrative since <time>; the session ended without /handoff'; make `romeu rm` and `recreate` (04 4.2) refuse on a TTY when the open generation has no `final` handoff and a sandbox is running, unless confirmed or given `--no-final-handoff`, so the decision is a prompt and not a memory.
findings.cost: One output rule, one TTY confirmation, one flag, test rows; a decision on the flag.

findings.defect: `julieta salvage --stop-agents` sends SIGTERM to Claude Code, which fires SessionEnd, which runs `julieta handoff write --facts` (git reads in every repo) concurrently with salvage step 2; the hook's julieta process is not among the agent's process names, so the SIGKILL does not reach it, and the ordering is unspecified.
findings.scenario: During `romeu rm`, the facts hook is computing dirty counts while salvage creates its temporary-index commit; the hook takes `index.lock` for a refresh, salvage's git call fails on the lock, and the worktree is reported `unreadable`, so `rm` exits 5 for a reason that has nothing to do with the work - or the facts file lands in the memory dir after the manifest was written.
findings.change: In 08 8.5 step 1 state that salvage waits for the agent's SessionEnd hook to finish (or kills julieta processes started by the agent's hooks too) before step 2, and that a facts handoff written during salvage is allowed and ignored by completeness; add the race to the container e2e (10 10.1, Concurrency).
findings.cost: One sentence and one concurrency test.

findings.defect: The candidate states (`awaiting`, `declined`, `superseded`) and the live spec commit are host records only; no manifest field, view file or julieta command lets the agent that authored a spec change learn its outcome.
findings.scenario: In the config sandbox the agent pushes `egress.extra: [api.stripe.com]` (J11); a day later it cannot tell whether the change is unsynced, awaiting approval, declined, or live, so it re-pushes, opens a second PR, or tells the user the domain is available when it is not.
findings.change: Add to the manifest (03 3.6) `specCommit` and, for the config project, nothing extra; add to `julieta status --json` (04 4.3) the project's live spec commit; and add to the view (13 13.6) or the manifest a closed record of the project's candidate state (none, awaiting, declined at <time>) with the gated field names, written by romeu at sync and approve.
findings.cost: Two manifest fields, one status section, one golden; a decision on where the candidate state lives.

findings.defect: No julieta command shows the effective egress allowlist or the gated domains still awaiting approval, and the manifest (03 3.6) does not carry them, so a blocked request reaches the agent only as sbx's proxy answer.
findings.scenario: The agent runs `go get` for a module whose host is not in the derived set; it receives a 403 from the proxy, has no way to know whether the host is unknown, gated and pending, or approved and not yet applied, and spends turns changing proxy and git settings it was never meant to touch.
findings.change: Carry `egress: {auto, approvedGated, pendingGated}` in the manifest (03 3.6, inside the 32 KiB bound) and print it from `julieta status` (04 4.3); have every julieta network error name the host and say which of the three sets it is in and that the durable fix is a spec edit plus the gate (07 7.5).
findings.cost: One manifest field, one status section, an error-message rule.

findings.defect: J8 step 3 says running sandboxes 'already have the tool (installed from inside)', which contradicts 07 7.5: a new tool's domains are not in the sandbox's egress until the change merges into `ref` and `romeu sync` applies them, so step 1's `julieta install` fails.
findings.scenario: The agent adds `core:python` to `mise.toml` on a feature branch, runs `julieta lock` and `julieta install` as J8 step 1 says; both need pypi.org, which is not allowed; the journey the guide describes cannot be followed, and the agent concludes the tool is broken.
findings.change: Rewrite J8: step 1 edits `mise.toml` and `julieta lock` only when the tool's domains are already allowed; otherwise the agent adds the tool, commits, opens the PR, and installs after the operator's sync (or the spec carries a gated `egress.tools` entry first); say in 07 7.5 that egress follows `ref`, so a tool added on a branch cannot be installed until it merges, and put that sentence in `julieta install`'s error.
findings.cost: Rewording of J8 and one sentence in 07 7.5; the J8 guide follows.

findings.defect: Several validation rules read host settings (`gitHosts`, `workloadRepositories`, `name@project` bindings), which `julieta spec validate` cannot see, and the spec does not say which rules are host-only, so a spec that validates in the sandbox fails `sync` with exit 2 and the agent hears it second-hand.
findings.scenario: The agent adds a repo on gitlab.com and `secrets: [npm]`; `julieta spec validate` exits 0; the operator's `romeu sync` exits 2 twice (unknown git host, then missing `npm@foo`), each a round trip through a person.
findings.change: Tag each rule in `rules.go` (03, opening) as `sandbox` or `host`; have `julieta spec validate` print a fixed line listing the host-only rules it did not check, and the generated rule table in `docs/reference/` show the column.
findings.cost: One field per rule, one output line, one generated column.

findings.defect: The appending julieta commands (`memory add`, `handoff write`, `event add`) are not safe to retry and their success output is unspecified (`--json` is promised for read commands only), so an agent whose tool call timed out cannot tell whether the write landed.
findings.scenario: `julieta memory add` runs while the store lock is held by another julieta process; the agent's tool call times out, the agent retries, and both calls complete: two identical entries, both printed at every SessionStart from then on.
findings.change: In 04 4.1 require each appending julieta command to print, in text and with `--json`, what it wrote (id and path), and to accept an optional caller key (`--key <ulid>`) stored with the write, so a second call with the same key returns the first result and writes nothing; add both to the idempotency meta-test (10 10.1).
findings.cost: One flag and one output rule on three commands, meta-test rows.

findings.defect: Every julieta command that exits non-zero emits `command-failed`, usage errors (exit 2 for a bad flag) included, so the agent's typos become permanent, undeletable ledger entries indistinguishable from real failures.
findings.scenario: An agent exploring the CLI runs `julieta memory show --josn` and five other malformed calls; six `command-failed` entries with `ref` set to a usage error id enter the ledger for good, and the lessons loop (13 13.9) counts a 'memory show' failure trend that never existed.
findings.change: In 13 13.2 exclude exit status 2 caused by flag or argument parsing (a named subset of error ids) from `command-failed`, or give those events a distinct closed `ref`; list the excluded ids in the generated table.
findings.cost: One rule and one table filter; a decision on which.

findings.defect: The ledger's in-session consumer is `julieta event list`, which the agent must remember to run, and the view changes only at ingest (13 13.6), so within a session the agent's own failures are invisible and 'no failures' looks the same as 'not ingested yet'.
findings.scenario: A `julieta install` failure and two hook failures happen this session; the agent runs `julieta event list` to check what went wrong, sees nothing new, and concludes everything ran clean.
findings.change: Have `julieta event list` (04 4.3) print the count of spool files not yet listed in `keys`, and have SessionStart (08 8.2) print the project's last N own failures from the view within the L5-1 bound; state in 13 13.9 that the lessons loop is fed by the hook, not by memory.
findings.cost: One count line, one section of hook output.

findings.defect: The free-text note is deferred until 'an agent needs to record something no id expresses, and the need is written as an issue', but the closed sets of `tool` and `ref` (13 13.2) cover julieta's own failures, not what an agent observes, and nothing tells the agent that an issue is the channel, so the trigger cannot fire.
findings.scenario: An agent finds that a guide step is wrong and a test flakes on arm64; `julieta event add` accepts only a command name, catalog key or id, so it records nothing, does not know to open an issue, and the deferral waits forever on an event its only observer was never told about.
findings.change: Make the trigger observable: `julieta event add` with no flag prints a fixed hint naming the issue path, the julieta skill says the same, and the row's trigger becomes 'the first issue labelled for it, or the first `note` with `tool: other` and no `ref`'.
findings.cost: One help line, one skill sentence, a reworded row.

findings.defect: An event carries no diagnosis and nothing joins a memory `lesson` entry to an event key, so the mechanical record of a failure and the agent's judgment of it are stored apart, unjoined.
findings.scenario: The agent diagnoses that a `hook-failed` came from a missing tool in CI and writes a `lesson` entry; months later the maintainer querying the ledger sees the event with no link to the explanation, and the lesson has no link back.
findings.change: Allow a memory entry's front matter (03 3.9) to carry a list of own-project ledger keys, validated against the view's `keys`, and have `julieta event list` show the entry ids that cite each key.
findings.cost: One optional field, one validation, one output column.

findings.defect: There are two lesson stores - `docs/lessons.md` (checked by `tools/ci lessons`) and memory entries tagged `lesson` (08 8.1) - and only the second is ever shown to the agent, so the record ADR 0003 says carries the project's shared memory is never delivered to the session that needs it.
findings.scenario: A lesson 'never run mise exec in tools/ci' sits in `docs/lessons.md`; a new session working on the product repo sees only memory entries at SessionStart, never reads the file, and reintroduces the pattern; the review catches it a round later.
findings.change: Either state in 12 12.7 and 08 8.1 that the two are one concept with two homes and have SessionStart print the titles of `docs/lessons.md` entries of the repo when the file exists (within the L5-1 bound), or merge them; in both cases name in 01 1.7 which word means which.
findings.cost: A decision, one hook output section or a vocabulary row.

findings.defect: Memory caps name 10 000 entries and 'per-dir size caps' without numbers for `handoff/`, while a facts file is written at every session end and every `/clear`; either normal agent activity eventually trips a cap that makes `sync` and `run` refuse (exit 2), or the handoff dir grows without bound.
findings.scenario: A project used daily for a year accumulates thousands of facts files; the next `romeu run` exits 2 naming the handoff dir as a layout violation, and the operator cannot start the sandbox to fix it, because the fix (julieta) runs inside it.
findings.change: In 08 8.1 state the handoff count and size caps as starting values, and say that julieta, not the caps, keeps `handoff/` under them by deleting facts files older than the newest K that no narrative depends on; a violation of the handoff cap warns and never refuses `run`.
findings.cost: Two starting values, one pruning rule in julieta, a test.

findings.defect: A handoff and a memory entry go to 'the memory dir of the repo containing the agent's cwd', and which repo `handoff show --hook` reads in a multi-repo project is unstated, so cross-repo work is filed by wherever the shell happens to be.
findings.scenario: The agent starts in shop-api, works in shop-web through `cd`, and records an entry about shop-web; it lands in shop-api's store, and a later session started in shop-web never sees it.
findings.change: In 08 8.2 and 04 4.3 make `--hook` read every manifest repo's memory (entries labelled by repo, within the bound) and make `memory add` print which repo it filed under.
findings.cost: Two sentences, one output label.

findings.defect: `julieta setup` fast-forwards the checked-out clean default branch, and a second `romeu run` on a running sandbox reruns setup while the agent works (the lock is released before `exec`, 04 4.1); the agent's HEAD moves and the report goes only to the host terminal.
findings.scenario: The agent has just read a file on main to plan an edit; the operator attaches a second terminal with `romeu run`; setup fast-forwards main underneath, and the agent's edit applies to content it never read.
findings.change: In 04 4.3 skip the fast-forward when an agent process (the profile's names) is running, or record the moved heads in julieta state so the next SessionStart and `julieta status` show 'default branch moved by setup'.
findings.cost: One condition or one warning.

findings.defect: The token-narrowing row, also stated in 05 5.4, returns to the operator 'every 2 autonomous work sessions', a count no mechanism keeps: v1 records no session start or end (the row on more event types says so), so the trigger lives in memory, which the first principle calls a defect.
findings.scenario: Six sessions pass; nobody counted; the token keeps the operator's full reach for weeks longer than the operator decided, and nothing shows the review was due.
findings.change: Give the trigger a producer: the handoff skill's checkpoint, or `julieta handoff write --final`, emits a closed `note` with a fixed `ref`, and a `tools/ci` or `romeu status` line counts them since the last review; or reword the trigger to an event that is already observable.
findings.cost: One `ref` member and one counter line, or a reworded trigger; an operator decision.

findings.defect: The row 'the review interval of the token narrowing' repeats the interval already stated in the row above, and its trigger 'the operator saying so' is not an observable event in the sense of ADR 0005 rule 3.
findings.scenario: A reader updates the interval in one row and not the other; the two rows disagree.
findings.change: Fold the interval into the token-narrowing row and delete the second row, or keep it with a trigger that names an event (the first review whose cost the panel or ledger reports).
findings.cost: One row removed or reworded.

findings.defect: ADR 0007's threat model defers two escapes (an untracked `go.work`, a caller `GOFLAGS` such as `-overlay`) until the hook next changes or Q25 is decided, citing a plan row and 'block O1 item d'; the deferral has no row in the index's Deferred decisions, and Q25 is decided (ADR 0008), so its trigger fired and nothing acted.
findings.scenario: A future reader of the index sees no such deferral; the escapes stay open after their reopening event; a cold reader of ADR 0007 cannot resolve 'the plan's deferred-decisions row'.
findings.change: Add the row to index: Deferred decisions with what holds until then, record that its Q25 trigger fired on 2026-10-07, and make the decision now (or restate the remaining trigger, the next change to `.githooks/pre-push`).
findings.cost: One row and a decision; an ADR change needs the approval line.

findings.defect: Q25 is decided yet still a row, against the table's own rule that a question leaves when it is settled.
findings.scenario: A reader counts open questions and gets one too many; `tools/ci acceptance` may look for a probe in its Settled-by cell.
findings.change: Remove Q25 now and leave its pointer in ADR 0008, or write the exception into the table's rule.
findings.cost: One row.

findings.defect: ADR 0005 accepts that 'nothing else reminds anyone' of a trigger outside review rounds, yet several triggers are machine-detectable (`doctor`'s size warning, a golangci-lint bump in `mise.toml`, `romeuMs` over the S8 budget); watching them is mechanical and left to memory.
findings.scenario: `doctor` warns about ledger size for months; the rotation decision it reopens is never taken, because no one connected the warning to the row.
findings.change: Give each machine-detectable trigger a fixed text in the output that detects it ('reopens deferred decision: <row>'), held equal to the row by `tools/ci sequences`.
findings.cost: A column or tag per row and a check.

findings.defect: `tools/ci` has no machine-readable output, no error ids and no exit-code table, unlike 04 4.1; its refusals are prose addressed to 'the operator' even when the pusher is an agent, and the pre-push `fast` takes minutes with no progress output, beyond a typical agent tool timeout.
findings.scenario: The agent pushes; the hook runs for four minutes; the agent's tool call times out at two and reports the push as failed; the agent retries, now racing the first run's judging step, and the second run refuses because HEAD 'moved'.
findings.change: Give `tools/ci` the error-table discipline of 04 4.1 (ids, fix hints, `--json`), address fix hints to 'the pusher', print one progress line per step, and state in 10 10.2 the expected run time and that an agent runs the push in the background.
findings.cost: An error table for tools/ci and a progress writer; a few words.

findings.defect: A forbidden-name hit is reported by file and line only, a two-segment entry can match two unrelated adjacent words, and no escalation is defined, so an agent that cannot see the name must reword by trial pushes that each take minutes.
findings.scenario: A commit message line with twelve words is refused; the agent rewrites it three times, each a multi-minute pre-push, and the third rewrite still holds the two words that happen to form the halves.
findings.change: In 10 10.2 state that after one refused rewrite the agent stops and hands the location to the operator, and print the matched segment count per hit, which leaks nothing the line does not already hold.
findings.cost: A sentence and one output field.

findings.defect: Done requires `go run ./tools/ci all`, but the spec never says which of its steps can run inside an agent's sandbox: `license` pulls a container image, the container and hybrid e2e need a Docker daemon and network for the base image, mise and herdr, and `vulnerabilities` reads the Go vulnerability database.
findings.scenario: The agent finishes a task, runs `all` in its sandbox, and `license` and the e2e fail on blocked registry hosts; it either reports done with failing steps or stalls; the maintainer learns the hosts one at a time.
findings.change: In 10 10.8 list the steps that run in a sandbox and the exact hosts and Docker access they need (one `sbx policy allow` set), and say what an agent reports when a step cannot run there ('not run: <step>, <reason>').
findings.cost: A short table and one sentence.

findings.defect: The PR body sections, the Middleware line, the golden list and the approval lines are all typed by the agent and checked only by `tools/ci pr` on a saved payload of an existing PR, so the first feedback arrives after the PR is public.
findings.scenario: The agent opens a PR missing an approval line for `checks`; `pr` fails in CI on the public PR; the body is edited twice more in public.
findings.change: Let `tools/ci pr` take a draft title and body file plus the local base..HEAD range (10 10.2), so the same check runs before `gh pr create`.
findings.cost: One input mode of an existing check.

findings.defect: Rule 1 excludes `SKILL.md`, rule 13 checks commands in README and guides only, and rule 16 is review, so the skills - the only documents written for the agent - fall under no rule of the documentation standard (plan T078 adds a command-name test the spec does not require).
findings.scenario: A julieta flag is renamed; the handoff skill still tells the agent to pipe into the old form; `tools/ci docs` passes; every `/handoff` fails until someone notices.
findings.change: Add a rule to ADR 0001, or extend rule 13, so `skills/*/SKILL.md` command lines are checked against the command definitions (flags included) and the headings the handoff skill names against `handoff write`'s validator.
findings.cost: A superseding ADR or rule amendment, one check in `tools/ci docs`.

findings.defect: The token row accepts merges, `v*` tags and ruleset edits as process only against the agent, but the spec does not consider the cheap deterministic guard against mistakes (not attacks): a `julieta-claude` PreToolUse rule refusing `gh pr merge`, a `v*` tag push and ruleset API calls without an explicit approval.
findings.scenario: An agent told 'ship it' merges its own PR through `gh pr merge`; nothing in the session stops it; the working agreement held only in the agent's reading of its instructions.
findings.change: Add to the row's mitigation a PreToolUse refusal in the `julieta-claude` kit (06 6.4) for those commands, stated as a guard against mistakes only.
findings.cost: One hook entry and its test; a decision.

findings.defect: ADR 0008 names 'issue and PR text, fetched pages and dependencies can steer the agent' as a class of the token's reach, but 05 5.4 has no residual-risk row for it and no mitigation.
findings.scenario: A PR comment instructs the agent to add a domain to `egress.extra` and push; the gate catches the widening, but the same text could ask for a merge, which nothing catches (L5-32).
findings.change: Add the row to 05 5.4 with what limits it (the gates, the review) and what does not.
findings.cost: One table row.

findings.defect: Sources of truth and trust boundaries model only what flows from the sandbox to the host; what the agent is entitled to know, and through which surface (manifest, view, hook output, command), is no class, so 'nothing the agent needs is hidden' has no owner and L5-9, L5-10 and L5-15 have no home.
findings.scenario: Each new feature decides ad hoc whether the agent sees its state; the gate, egress and ledger each chose 'host only' by default.
findings.change: Add a row to 01 1.2, 'Host facts the agent reads', listing each fact, its surface and its freshness (manifest at exec, view at ingest, hook at session start), and a sentence in the index principle that the agent consumes these results.
findings.cost: One table row and one sentence.

findings.defect: Every journey is told from the operator's side; none shows what the agent sees when its context is compacted, its request is blocked by egress, its push is refused, or its spec change is pending at the gate.
findings.scenario: The scenario functions and guides cover none of these, so no test catches a regression in what the agent is told.
findings.change: Add one journey (or J5 variants) for the agent's side, with its steps as [J] and [A] and assertions on the hook and command output.
findings.cost: One journey, one scenario function, one guide page.

findings.defect: The plan says its source of truth includes 'the seven decision records under `adr/`', but there are eight; its rule that counts are 'kept true by hand' is the mechanical-in-memory defect and has already drifted.
findings.scenario: An implementer trusts the count and misses ADR 0008.
findings.change: Remove hand-kept counts or check them in `tools/ci`.
findings.cost: A few words or a small check.

findings.defect: T059 has no acceptance for a SessionStart bound or hook failure behavior, T078's test checks command names but not flags or headings, and T079 has no test that a personal kit cannot unwire the hooks.
findings.scenario: Each of L5-1, L5-3, L5-4 and L5-31 lands in the spec with no plan task that tests it.

postmortem: v1.0.0 shipped; the host side held - no host code ran, no secret leaked, salvage lost no branch - and the product still failed the agents it was built around. SessionStart printed every entry, lesson and hook failure in no fixed order and flooded the window; compaction, which no hook covered, then summarized it away, and the narrative handoff depended on the operator typing /handoff (08 8.2, 03 3.9, 08 8.3, J5, J6, 11 C3/C5). Agents authored specs and never learned whether they were synced, awaiting or declined, and J8 promised an install that egress forbade until merge and sync (00 0.1, 01 1.6, 03 3.6, 07 7.5, J8). The network was a wall without a map: a bare 403 outside julieta install (04 4.3, 07 7.5). A personal kit unwired the hooks, and nothing noticed after the one B2 measurement (06 6.4, 06 6.5, S5). The ledger recorded failures the agent never read, filled with permanent entries from typos, with no place for the agent's diagnosis (13 13.2, 13 13.6, 13 13.9). Retried writes duplicated, and silent success could not be verified (04 4.1). Building the product in its own sandbox was harder still: minutes-long pre-push beyond tool timeouts, prose refusals for 'the operator', unlocatable forbidden-name hits, a done that default egress could not reach, PR text checked only once public (10 10.2, 10 10.8, 12 12.4). And the unsaid: agents merged because the token could and nothing in the session said no (05 5.4, ADR 0008); nobody counted two autonomous sessions (index: Deferred decisions); a deferral with a fired trigger sat in ADR 0007 with no row; docs/lessons.md was never read because only the other lesson store was shown (12 12.7, 08 8.1). The common cause: the spec made the agent's outputs deterministic and left its inputs to chance.
lens_critique: This lens treats the agent as the user to be served, but for this product the agent is also the adversary of 05, and several of my findings (show the agent its egress, its gate state, other projects' events) widen what an agent learns; the security model may rightly prefer the agent to know less, and the lens has no way to weigh that. It also assumes one agent behavior (Claude Code, a given hook API, compaction), so findings tied to the pinned version's hook semantics may be wrong until a probe measures them, and it over-weights the agent's comfort against the operator's time: each fact made visible in the sandbox is a mechanism the one maintainer must keep true.
missing_viewpoint: The operator who reviews and approves the agent's work at the gate and the PR - the human in the loop whose attention every mechanism spends (L1 uses the tool, L14 is on duty, but no lens judges the approval and review load as the scarce resource the gates and ADR 0008 lean on).
